memories.content: Specify the order and recipients for reporting serious discomfort during the study.
Field staff rely on a pre-defined contact sequence when serious discomfort is reported.
Establish criteria for halting the use of a design alternative if recurring severe errors appear during formative evaluation.
Do not include a design alternative halted for safety reasons in subsequent evaluation iterations without modification.
Even in controlled environments, delayed prototype recovery procedures increase session interruption time and alter data collection conditions for the same task.
Calculate user research compensation budgets based on the estimated participation burden, combining session time with required technical and travel preparation.
Compensate participants who withdraw from the study midway for their actual participation time.
Compensate for the time actually spent in sessions, regardless of the research modality.
Allow the issuance of gift cards of equivalent value to participants in remote studies who cannot use electronic transfers.
Do not treat an unresolved payment method as a deficiency at the proposal stage.
Allow differential compensation amounts for on-site and remote studies when participation burden varies due to travel or technical preparation.
Participants judge the fairness of compensation based on the combined burden of session time and required technical and travel preparation.
In longitudinal studies requiring diary entries and repeated reporting, include out-of-session recording time in compensation calculations.
Distinguish between participant research compensation and labor costs for field staff performing installation and operational support as part of their duties.
The user tends to count session time but omit participants’ advance setup and follow-up reporting time.

analysis.overview: The frames cover separate operational domains. The reference addresses discomfort escalation, safety-based design iteration controls, and prototype recovery effects; the compared frame addresses participant compensation principles, exceptions, payment methods, modality and longitudinal burdens, staff-cost boundaries, and common budgeting omissions.

relations.reason: The reference memories state complementary parts of one escalation procedure, while the compared frame contains no claim about discomfort reporting.
relations.summary: Serious discomfort during a study should be handled through a predefined reporting sequence identifying the order and recipients.

relations.reason: This is an independently useful reference-only safety threshold; the compared frame addresses compensation rather than design-halting criteria.
relations.summary: Formative evaluation should define criteria for halting a design alternative when severe errors recur.

relations.reason: This reference-only rule governs subsequent reuse after a safety halt and has no counterpart in the compensation material.
relations.summary: A design alternative halted for safety reasons should not return unchanged in later evaluation iterations.

relations.reason: This reference-only observation concerns recovery delays and session conditions, which the compared frame does not address.
relations.summary: Delayed prototype recovery increases interruption time and changes data-collection conditions even in controlled environments.

relations.reason: The compared memories provide the policy and its participant-centered rationale as parts of one burden-based compensation claim; the reference frame contains no compensation policy.
relations.summary: Compensation budgets should reflect the combined burden of session time and required technical and travel preparation, consistent with participants’ fairness judgments.

relations.reason: The compared memories state a general actual-time rule and its withdrawal application; the reference frame contains no corresponding compensation claim.
relations.summary: Participants should be compensated for time actually spent in sessions across modalities, including when they withdraw midway.

relations.reason: This is an independently useful compared-only payment-method alternative with no reference-side counterpart.
relations.summary: Remote-study participants unable to use electronic transfers may receive gift cards of equivalent value.

relations.reason: This compared-only rule concerns proposal-stage assessment and is distinct from selecting an eventual payment alternative.
relations.summary: An unresolved payment method should not be treated as a deficiency at the proposal stage.

relations.reason: This compared-only policy specifically permits burden-based modality differentials, a decision not addressed by the reference frame.
relations.summary: On-site and remote studies may use different compensation amounts when travel or technical preparation creates different participation burdens.

relations.reason: This compared-only rule adds a longitudinal, out-of-session burden category not discussed in the reference frame.
relations.summary: Compensation calculations for longitudinal studies should include time spent on diary entries and repeated reporting outside sessions.

relations.reason: This compared-only accounting boundary concerns different recipients and cost types and has no reference-side counterpart.
relations.summary: Participant research compensation should be distinguished from labor costs for field staff performing installation and operational support duties.

relations.reason: This compared-only observation identifies a specific budgeting omission; the reference frame provides no related assessment.
relations.summary: Compensation planning commonly risks counting session time while omitting participants’ advance setup and follow-up reporting time.

reports.compared_only: Compared-only material covers burden- and time-based compensation, withdrawal handling, payment flexibility, modality and longitudinal adjustments, separation of participant and staff costs, and budgeting omissions.
reports.reference_only: Reference-only material covers serious-discomfort escalation, safety thresholds and restrictions for design alternatives, and the effects of delayed prototype recovery.
